answer: A burn registry makes every identity cost real money. The agent burns 500 POA and the registry records the receipt. That receipt binds the identity to one hardware key, so one machine holds one seat. Every action must carry that key's signature, so a second identity needs a second machine and another 500 POA burn. An attacker chasing 100 fake agents must burn 50,000 POA and buy 100 devices, about $30,000 in hardware and $12,000 in burned tokens. A river cuts one channel through rock; each identity crosses one narrow ledge, and to forge a second path means digging a new riverbed.
